newsitem.title: USA: Neoprobe sees return to profits in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Neoprobe sees return to profits in 1998.

text.p: Neoprobe Corp expects to become profitable in the second half of 1998, according to President and Chief Operating Officer David Bupp.

"Analysts have us reaching profitability in the second half of 1998 and this is consistent with our internal (expectations)," said Bupp at the New York Society of Security Analysts' Health Care Industry Conference.

Bupp said that getting into the black is dependent on approval of the company's RIGScan CR49, a surgical cancer detection drug, in the U.S. and Europe by the end of 1997. He said the company expects to receive approvals for the RIGScan CR49 in both the U.S. and Europe this year.
Neoprobe submitted a Biologic License Application to the U.S. FDA for CR49 for the intraoperative detection of metastatic colorectal cancer in December 1996.
